shrunkBy.wave: M49.R2 2026-09-24 — rust's two name-set tests become char scans (#798)
shrunkBy.note: A row may only disappear when the source no longer holds the regex. Both removals are code fixes, not reclassifications: `/\b(Serialize|Deserialize)\b/` and `/\b(Parser|Subcommand|Args|ValueEnum)\b/` were name-set tests on a `#[derive(...)]` / clap attribute argument's TEXT, and the test only ever needed WORD-RUN MEMBERSHIP — which is what `hasBareWord` computes with a char-code scan, exactly the class of replacement the policy's rule 2 asks for (char-scan with an inline equivalence proof). The inline proof is on `hasBareWord` in the analyzer; the corpus proof is script/m14/tmp/rust-004-regex-equivalence.ts (1,481 files, 970 bodies, 0 mismatches between the two regexes and the scan). Rust is now a zero-regex lane.

shrunkBy.wave: M60 clojure deep round 2026-09-28 — the clojure lane becomes ZERO-REGEX (CLJ-D20)
shrunkBy.note: A row may only disappear when the source no longer holds the regex, and this one is a CODE FIX, not a reclassification: `/^%(\d+|&)?$/` tested a Clojure anonymous-argument shorthand (`%`, `%1`..`%N`, `%&`) against a symbol's name string, and it is now `isAnonArgShorthand`, a char walk. The conversion is PROVED, not asserted — script/m14/tmp/clj-regex-equiv.ts runs the regex and the scan over every sym_lit name in three corpora (633 files, 187,678 symbol nodes, 13,363 distinct names) plus a 42-case adversarial battery and reports 0 mismatches. The row's own note said 'mechanically convertible to a structural symbol-name check; NOT converted in this wave because the clojure analyzer is its authoring lane's file' — that reason expired when the file became this lane's authoring lane. reviews/regex-policy.md's clojure table is updated to 0 in the same commit, and script/m12/regex-census.ts is re-run from HEAD blobs (the 2026-09-12 W6 rule) so the census cannot keep describing a regex the code no longer holds. Record: reviews/clojure/deep-review-2026-09-28.md, finding CLJ-D20; fixtures clojure/anon-shorthand; mutant clojure/anon-shorthand-greedy (CAUGHT).

The row is removed because the SOURCE is gone, not because it was reclassified. The regex sat on the declared-type path, where the receiver can only be an `identifier` node's text: on a plain identifier (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, no `<or>`, no `=`) all three surgeries on that line are provable no-ops, and on a QUOTED identifier it CORRUPTED a legitimate name. Measured over the three pinned zig corpora (3,839 files): 34,132 quoted identifiers, 31,349 of them in a type position, and 1,348 of those carrying a character from the junk class - the upstream C compiler's own diagnostics included (`aro/Diagnostics.zig:33` `@"fatal error"` was published as `@"fatalerror"`, and `@"*"` as `@""`). The replacement is to publish the source spelling, which is what every other surface of the analyzer already publishes (symbol names, `uses` field leaves, call leaves), so edges still resolve inside the index; the two surviving tests are a `Set` membership and a character-code range. Evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/zig/declared-type-leaf (expects `@"weird type"`, FORBIDS the corrupted `@"weirdtype"`), mutation zig/quoted-identifier-mangled, validation/m12/results/zig-deep-review.json, and the equivalence argument plus the population counts above. The lane is now zero-regex.
